prose: Basis: the linked page returned only site boilerplate rather than article text, so this note rests on the Hacker News headline and yesterday's reporting. The r/opensource story has jumped from The Verge to the wider tech press: the subreddit's moderators banned projects that use AI, are made by AI, or are intended for AI, and - in the same rules refresh - told non-English speakers to find another community because AI-written and AI-translated text cannot be told apart. The revolt in the community and the rival r/trueopensource subreddit continue to grow.
highlights: The r/opensource AI ban story spread to wider tech press via Hacker News
Rules bar projects using, made by, or intended for AI - and effectively exclude non-English speakers
Moderators say they cannot distinguish AI-written from AI-translated text
The linked page yielded only boilerplate; note based on the headline and prior coverage
